title: Also so much credit should go to Danya Taymor’s amazing direction- so...
transcript: I am not exaggerating when I say the final, like, 30 to 40 minutes of this musical is some of my favorite theater I have ever seen. And it's really interesting because coming out of Act 1, I was really unsure about how I felt about this musical. Like, don't get me wrong, I certainly enjoyed Act 1, and I thought the performances were really great. There are some great rectorial moments. But I just couldn't shake this feeling that maybe this should have been a play, because it's very theatrical. Like, I see why they wanted to adapt the story for the stage, but as for why they wanted to specifically make it a musical, I wasn't entirely sure. There's certainly a couple of standout moments. I really loved the opening number. Uh, the song Great Expectations. I think it's really strong. But the other songs, while good songs, like, I really enjoy the style of music that they chose to use for this musical. The songs themselves didn't really feel like they added anything to the storytelling. In fact, they almost slowed down the pacing of the act. And I felt like just cutting the songs and maybe replacing them with a short book scene would have been more effective. But I say all of that to circle back around to Act two, which really made me understand, okay, this is why they decided to make it a musical. And there were two songs in particular that I Was just floored by those being the solo that they give to Dallas, the leader of the greasers, in Act 2, as well as the song Stay Gold sung by Johnny, which I believe is on Spotify if you wanna listen to it. It's a really good song. And it's those two songs in particular, along with a couple of really cool sequences and a great finale, that I think make Act 2 so strong. And that made me realize that, like, this is what I wanted from Act one. And so I hope that over the course of previous, because they are still in previous, they only just started performances last weekend, they're able to make those changes to Act one because the bones of the show are so good. And when the show is good, it is great. Like, by the end, I was genuinely more moved by the show than I was the notebook. So if they are able to make the changes that they need to change, this is the potential to not only win Best Musical this season, but I think be a long running modern classic. But they gotta tighten up that first act.
